deployBuild: It only handles hosting[] and does NOT handle the cloudbaserc app resource — app artifacts must be built by you in the project directory (read the build command and output directory from deployPlan's buildHint), or use the CLI `tcb app deploy` for a cloud build instead.
The build is a purely local operation: it resolves no environment, requires no login and needs no confirm.
deployPlan: ⚠️ app / hosting plan items are always a direct upload of existing artifacts: declarative deploy deploys but never builds;
buildCommand / framework in cloudbaserc are only used to infer the output directory and are never executed.

app / hosting plan items carry buildHint = { buildCommand, outputDir, artifactReady } (machine-readable — do not parse the localized text in details): artifactReady=false means the output directory is missing or empty, and deployApply is guaranteed to fail (BUILD_OUTPUT_NOT_FOUND).
Re-run deployPlan afterwards to confirm artifactReady=true;
do not edit the config to work around it.
deployApply: It is a write operation that changes cloud resources and requires an explicit confirm=true to execute.
It is recommended to preview with deployPlan first and execute after confirming the plan.
⚠️ Deploys but never builds: this tool runs no build command at all (neither app nor hosting).
buildCommand / installCommand / framework in cloudbaserc are only used to infer the output directory and are never executed.
do not edit the config to work around it.
- confirm: must be explicitly true to execute the deployment, otherwise it is rejected

- confirmDestructive: when the pending database migrations contain destructive statements (DROP/TRUNCATE/DELETE, ALTER…DROP/RENAME), besides confirm, confirmDestructive=true must also be explicitly passed to execute;
otherwise it is rejected and the matched migrations and statements are listed.
